message.content: {"accepted": true, "issues": [], "assessment": "The candidate proposes a single replace_text action on timebook.py with a base_sha256 matching the observed file digest (14c86f2ce77892ebd7b49a9baf9155f6b5ed4b75d4207bcdda3f29ca88056dbd). The old string is an exact substring of the observed timebook.py content, and the new string adds explicit validation of the UTC offset hours/minutes before datetime.fromisoformat, which directly targets the reported bug that invalid offsets like +00:60, +00:99, -00:60, +24:00, +99:00 are accepted. The regex ISO_RE already restricts the offset shape to [+-]\\d{2}:\\d{2}, so slicing text[-6:] is safe for matched inputs, and the added check rejects out-of-range hh/mm. This is a grounded, appropriately scoped edit that can advance the goal; it does not modify tests. Uncertainties: whether datetime.fromisoformat would already reject some of these offsets on the running Python version is not verified here, but the explicit guard is harmless and correct; actual test execution is a separate gate.", "claims": []}
